lines.keys: Trailing digits pulled from book_id and purchase_id and cast to int; the two tables are joined on that shared number.
lines.rank: Decades ordered by average rating, highest first; limit 1; no tie-break.
lines.parse: Year = four digits after the first month name, allowing an optional day and comma, taken from details, else from subtitle. Bare four-digit numbers are ignored.
lines.shape: One row, one column: the decade as an integer start year, e.g. 1990, unrounded.
lines.filter: Books with no parsed year are dropped; the inner join keeps only books that have reviews; HAVING-style outer filter keeps decades with at least 10 distinct books.
lines.metric: Decade = year integer-divided by 10, times 10. Per decade: count of distinct books and the mean rating over individual reviews.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info (book_id, details prose with the publication date, subtitle as fallback); bookreview_review (purchase_id, rating per review).

lines.keys: The trailing number of book_id ('bookid_N') is matched to the trailing number of purchase_id ('purchaseid_N'). Both are extracted with a digits-at-end pattern and cast to integer.
lines.rank: Sorted by title ascending. There is no limit and no tie-break.
lines.parse: Categories: the quoted element "Literature & Fiction" is matched inside the JSON-like string. Language: the word English as a whole word anywhere in details, so bilingual English editions also count.
lines.shape: One column, title, with one row per matching book. A title containing a comma is wrapped in double quotes, with inner quotes doubled (CSV style).
lines.filter: Keep books whose categories contain the quoted Literature & Fiction element, whose details mention English as a whole word, and whose average rating equals exactly 5.
lines.metric: The average of individual review ratings for each book number, grouped in a subquery before the join.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info supplies title, the categories string list and the details prose, which holds the language. bookreview_review supplies rating per purchase_id.

lines.keys: The trailing number of review purchase_id ('purchaseid_N') is matched to the trailing number of books book_id ('bookid_N'). Both are extracted with a trailing-digits regex and cast to int.
lines.rank: Ordered by average rating descending, then title ascending. No limit.
lines.parse: review_time is text shaped 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MI:SS' and cast to timestamp. categories is regex-searched for the quoted element "Children's Books".
lines.shape: One column (title), one row per qualifying book. Titles containing a comma are wrapped in double quotes and inner quotes are doubled, CSV-style.
lines.filter: Keeps reviews dated on or after 2020-01-01 and books whose categories contain the quoted Children's Books element. The book's windowed average rating must be at least …, inclusive.
lines.metric: Average rating over individual reviews in the window, grouped per book number, computed in a CTE before the join.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info gives the title and the categories text (a string-encoded list); bookreview_review gives the rating, review_time and purchase_id.

lines.keys: Ids trimmed with leading '#' stripped on both sides: transcript LeadId__c to lead Id, pricebookentry Product2Id to product Id; products matched by name appearing in call body.
lines.rank: Blocks ordered lead, transcripts, prices, rules; transcripts newest first, products alphabetical, rules by paragraph number; no limit.
lines.parse: Policy answers split on blank lines into paragraphs, keeping those starting with a number and period, whitespace collapsed; product name found by substring position in transcript text.
lines.shape: Four columns kind, ref_id, label, detail; many rows of evidence; lead detail concatenates title, company, status; price cast to text; BANT verdict left to reader.
lines.filter: Only the given lead; products named in its calls; articles whose summary equals title and title contains a whole word budget, authority, need or timeline.
lines.metric: none; evidence rows only, distinct product/price pairs, rule order numbers kept from split ordinality.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_lead for the lead; voicecalltranscript__c Body__c for calls; product2 names with pricebookentry UnitPrice; knowledge__kav faq_answer__c for policy rules.

lines.keys: Case ids, owner ids and history caseid/newvalue are trimmed and stripped of a leading '#'. Assignments join to in-window cases on the normalised case id.
lines.rank: Ascending by average handle time, ties broken by agent id ascending; limit 1.
lines.parse: Created and closed date strings are cast directly to timestamptz. The history field name is trimmed before comparing it to 'Owner Assignment'.
lines.shape: A single row with one column, the normalised agent id.
lines.filter: Cases created from four months before 2023-09-02 through the end of that day. Handle time uses only closed cases with at most one Owner Assignment. Eligible agents handled more than one distinct case.
lines.metric: An agent handles a case if it appears as an assignee or as the case owner (union). Handle time is closed minus created in seconds, credited to the owner and averaged per agent.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case gives case id, owner, created and closed dates; crmarenapro_casehistory__c gives Owner Assignment rows with case id and new owner value.

lines.keys: contact Id to the given contact; contact AccountId = order AccountId; orderitem OrderId = order Id; orderitem Product2Id = product Id. Every id is trimmed and has leading '#' stripped.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: EffectiveDate is trimmed and cast as a YYYY-MM-DD date. Product Name is tested for 'AI' as a whole word, case-sensitive, using word-boundary regex.
lines.shape: One column, the product id, trimmed and '#'-stripped. Distinct rows, possibly several.
lines.filter: Order date falls in the previous calendar month: on or after the first day of last month and before the first day of the current month, relative to the fixed today. Product name must contain the whole word AI.
lines.metric: No aggregate. Distinct normalised product ids are returned.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_contact gives the account; crmarenapro_order holds EffectiveDate; crmarenapro_orderitem links orders to products; crmarenapro_product2 holds Id and Name.

lines.keys: Opportunity.ContractID__c matches Contract.Id exactly, with whitespace trimmed and a leading '#' stripped on both sides. The join does not go through AccountId.
lines.rank: Agents are ordered by average cycle, lowest first, ties broken by agent Id ascending. Only the first is kept.
lines.parse: CreatedDate is cut to its first 10 characters and cast to a date. CompanySignedDate is a plain YYYY-MM-DD cast to a date. The OwnerId agent key is trimmed and has '#' stripped.
lines.shape: One row with a single column, Id: the agent's cleaned owner Id.
lines.filter: Keeps only opportunities whose contract's CompanySignedDate falls on or after April 1, 2023 and before May 1, 2023.
lines.metric: Per opportunity, the cycle is signed date minus created date in days. The average of those day counts is taken per agent (the opportunity owner).
lines.sources: crmarenapro_opportunity supplies the owner (OwnerId), the creation timestamp (CreatedDate) and the contract link (ContractID__c); crmarenapro_contract supplies Id and CompanySignedDate.

lines.keys: Order matches contract on account id plus contract start date equal to order effective date; order items match order on order id. All ids trimmed and leading '#' stripped.
lines.rank: Sales amount descending, ties broken by agent id ascending, limit 1.
lines.parse: Dates are trimmed 'YYYY-MM-DD' text, cast to date; Quantity and UnitPrice are text cast to numeric; start/effective dates compared as trimmed text.
lines.shape: One row, one column: the agent id, no rounding.
lines.filter: Keep contracts whose company signed date falls between five months before the fixed date 2022-11-25 and that date, inclusive; an order counts if any matching contract qualifies.
lines.metric: Distinct qualifying orders per owner; sum over their order items of quantity times unit price, grouped by agent id.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_contract (AccountId, StartDate, CompanySignedDate), crmarenapro_order (Id, OwnerId as agent, AccountId, EffectiveDate), crmarenapro_orderitem (OrderId, Quantity, UnitPrice).

lines.keys: Line items join product2 and pricebookentry by Id; every key has leading '#' and surrounding spaces stripped first. Quote id matched exactly after the same cleanup.
lines.rank: Quote lines first, ordered by product name; then policy rules, ordered by article title and paragraph position. No limit.
lines.parse: Article bodies split on blank lines into paragraphs, keeping those starting with a number and period; whitespace collapsed. Text quantity, prices, discount and total cast to numeric.
lines.shape: Many rows: kind, article id, title, product, quantity, list price, unit price, discount, total price, rule text. Fields that do not apply to a row are null. No rounding.
lines.filter: Only this quote's lines. Articles count when the summary equals the title or starts with the word 'policy'. A rule naming a catalog product is kept only if it names a product on this quote.
lines.metric: none: no aggregation. It lists line items and candidate rule paragraphs as evidence, and the violation is judged by reading them.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_quotelineitem for the quote's lines, product2 for names, pricebookentry for list price; knowledge__kav faq_answer__c body holds policy rules, with title and summary.

lines.keys: task.WhatId is matched to opportunity.Id. On both sides a leading '#' is stripped and surrounding spaces are trimmed before the ids are compared.
lines.rank: The opportunity row comes first, then the tasks by activity date ascending, with task id as the tie-break. There is no limit.
lines.parse: No pattern extraction. Text fields are only trimmed. The recorded stage gets a 'StageName: ' prefix and goes in the status column.
lines.shape: Many rows with the columns kind, id, activity_date, status, subject and description. There is no rounding. The final stage label is chosen by a human reading these rows.
lines.filter: Keeps only the opportunity whose normalised Id equals the given id, plus all tasks linked to it. There are no date window or status exclusions.
lines.metric: No aggregate. It stacks the opportunity row with its task rows as evidence, and a reader maps the latest task activity onto one of the five stages.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_opportunity supplies the Id, Name, StageName and CloseDate. crmarenapro_task supplies the Id, WhatId, ActivityDate, Status, Subject and Description.

lines.keys: Case orderitemid__c matches orderitem Id. Every id is trimmed and has leading '#' stripped first. Order items are chosen by exact match of normalised Product2Id to the given product id.
lines.rank: Months ordered by case count descending, earlier month first on ties. No limit, so every month is listed and the top row is the outlier.
lines.parse: createddate is read as an ISO timestamp with timezone, converted to UTC, then cut to a date for the window and to the start of the calendar month for grouping.
lines.shape: Many rows: the full month name without padding, plus the case count. The question wants only the month name, so the answer is the name in the top row.
lines.filter: Keeps only cases whose order item belongs to the product and whose UTC created date falls between today minus 10 months and today, both ends included.
lines.metric: Counts cases per calendar month of creation, grouped by month start.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case (orderitemid__c, createddate) holds the cases; crmarenapro_orderitem (Id, Product2Id) links each order item to its product.

lines.keys: Case orderitemid__c matches orderitem Id. Both sides, and Product2Id, are trimmed and have any leading '#' removed before comparing.
lines.rank: Sorts by case count, highest first, with no explicit tie-break, and keeps the top row.
lines.parse: createddate is ISO text with a +0000 offset. It is cast to timestamptz, converted to UTC and cut to a date. Issue ids are trimmed and a leading '#' is removed.
lines.shape: One row with one column, the normalised issue id.
lines.filter: Keeps order items whose Product2Id is the given product. Keeps cases created on or after today minus five months and on or before today, inclusive. Drops cases with no issue id.
lines.metric: Counts case rows for each normalised issue id.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case gives issueid__c, orderitemid__c and createddate. crmarenapro_orderitem gives Id and Product2Id, which connect cases to the product.

lines.keys: Joins line items to product and pricebook entry by Id; before matching, every id has leading '#' stripped and spaces trimmed. The quote id gets the same cleanup.
lines.rank: Quote lines come first, sorted by product name. Policy rules follow, sorted by article title, then paragraph number. No limit.
lines.parse: Text quantities and prices are cast to numeric. The article body is split on blank lines, keeping paragraphs that start with a number and a period; runs of whitespace become one space.
lines.shape: Many rows: kind, article_id, title, product, quantity, list_price, unit_price, discount, total_price, rule. Columns that do not apply are null. The violated article is chosen by reading the rows.
lines.filter: Keeps line items of the given quote. Keeps articles whose summary equals the title or starts with 'Policy'. Keeps rules naming no catalog product, or naming a product on this quote.
lines.metric: none; rows listed as evidence for a manual judgment, no aggregation
lines.sources: crmarenapro_quotelineitem for quantity, unit price, discount and total; crmarenapro_product2 for names; crmarenapro_pricebookentry for list price; crmarenapro_knowledge__kav title, summary and faq_answer__c policy text.

lines.keys: No cross-table join; transfer and handled aggregates are matched on agent id, each id and the case id trimmed with any leading '#' stripped, empty values turned to null.
lines.rank: Transfer count ascending, ties broken by agent id ascending, limit 1.
lines.parse: Date is the first ten characters of createddate, cast to a calendar date. Agent ids come from oldvalue__c and newvalue__c after trimming and removing '#'.
lines.shape: One row, one column "Id" holding the agent id.
lines.filter: Owner Assignment rows whose date is in the four complete quarters before the current quarter (start of current quarter minus 12 months, up to that start). Keep agents with at least one handled case.
lines.metric: Per agent, transfers = count of assignment rows naming them as old owner. Handled = distinct cases naming them as new owner. Only agents with at least one transfer are ranked (inner join).
lines.sources: crmarenapro_casehistory__c only: field__c marks 'Owner Assignment' rows, oldvalue__c the handing-off agent, newvalue__c the receiving agent, caseid__c the case, createddate the time.

lines.keys: Case accountid matches account Id after trimming whitespace and stripping any leading '#' on both sides.
lines.rank: States are ordered by average closure seconds, lowest first, with the state name breaking ties. Only the first row is kept.
lines.parse: Both timestamp texts are ISO strings with a +0000 offset, cast to timestamptz. The date part is the first ten characters, cast to date. ShippingState is trimmed.
lines.shape: One row with a single column: the state abbreviation.
lines.filter: Keep closed cases only (closeddate not null). The case must be created in the six full quarters before the current quarter: from 18 months before the current quarter start up to that start.
lines.metric: Per case, closure time is the exact seconds between created and closed timestamps. These are averaged per state.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case supplies createddate, closeddate and accountid. crmarenapro_account supplies Id and ShippingState, which serves as the case's state.

lines.keys: Package versions match project_packageversion on System NPM, Name and Version exactly; ProjectName lowercased matches the owner/repo read from Project_Information, also lowercased.
lines.rank: Order by stars descending, then by Name descending to break ties; limit 5.
lines.parse: From VersionInfo JSON, read Ordinal as an integer and check IsRelease; from Project_Information, read the first owner/repo token plus stars from 'stars count of N', 'starred by N', or 'N stars', commas removed.
lines.shape: Five rows with columns Name and Version; stars are not output.
lines.filter: Keep NPM rows whose IsRelease is true, and only the top row per package by highest Ordinal (nulls last). The joins drop packages without a matching project.
lines.metric: Per package name and latest version, take the max star count over its matched projects.
lines.sources: deps_dev_v1_packageinfo (System, Name, Version, VersionInfo JSON); deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion links versions to ProjectName; deps_dev_v1_project_info.Project_Information free text holds repo and stars.

lines.keys: packageinfo joins project_packageversion on System, Name, Version exactly; ProjectName lowercased matches the lowercased owner/repo token pulled from Project_Information.
lines.rank: Fork count descending, ties broken by ProjectName ascending, limited to 5.
lines.parse: Project owner/repo is the first slash-joined token, lowercased. Forks come from one of three phrasings: 'forks count of N', 'forked N times', 'N forks'. Commas stripped, cast to bigint.
lines.shape: Five rows with columns ProjectName, Version and ForksCount (an integer), no rounding.
lines.filter: Licenses JSON array contains 'MIT'; System is 'NPM'; VersionInfo IsRelease is true; only projects present in the MIT set.
lines.metric: Fork count per project, no aggregation. Each project keeps one release version: newest UpstreamPublishedAt, then highest Ordinal, then Version text descending (row_number = 1).
lines.sources: deps_dev_v1_project_info (Licenses JSON, free-text Project_Information holding repo name and forks); deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion links packages to ProjectName; deps_dev_v1_packageinfo gives System, VersionInfo, UpstreamPublishedAt.

lines.keys: files join contents on the blob id. Repo-level Python flags join to README rows on the exact repo_name. The language rows are limited to repos that have README files.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: Python is found as a language token: 'Python' followed by '(N bytes' or ', totaling N bytes'. Copyright is a case-insensitive match on 'copyright' or the © symbol.
lines.shape: One row with three columns: the total README count, the copyright README count and the unrounded proportion.
lines.filter: Keep a path only if its file name is README.md, in any case and at any directory depth, and the file has content. The repo must have a languages row, and none of its rows may name Python.
lines.metric: Each README file counts once. Count all of them, count those with copyright, then divide the copyright count by the total as a float, guarding against a zero total.
lines.sources: github_repos_files gives repo_name, path and blob id; github_repos_contents.content holds the README text; github_repos_languages.language_description is a free-text sentence naming each repo's languages.

lines.keys: Files join contents on an exact match of id. Repos join languages on an exact match of repo_name. Files are cut to one row per id before either join.
lines.rank: Sort by copy count, highest first. Break ties by repo_name, alphabetical. Keep one row.
lines.parse: Copy count is the first number before ' times' in the description, cast to integer. Swift is a language token followed by '(N bytes' or ', totaling N bytes'. Paths are matched case-insensitively for a '.swift' ending.
lines.shape: One row with one column, repo_name. The path is not output, even though the comment says it is.
lines.filter: Keep paths ending in .swift (any case) and descriptions containing the whole word 'non-binary' (any case). Keep only repos whose languages list Swift as a language token.
lines.metric: No aggregate. Each file row carries its own parsed copy count. DISTINCT ON id keeps the first repo_name and path in sort order.
lines.sources: github_repos_files gives id, repo_name and path; github_repos_contents.repo_data_description holds the copy count and binary flag; github_repos_languages.language_description lists each repo's languages.

lines.keys: Languages and licenses joined on exact repo_name to build a distinct repo list; commits then inner-joined to that list on repo_name.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: Language found by a case-sensitive substring match for 'Shell' inside the free-text language_description; no other text or JSON parsing.
lines.shape: One row, one column total_count holding the integer count.
lines.filter: License exactly 'apache-2.0' (lowercase); message not null, length strictly under 1000; lowercased message not starting with 'merge', 'update' or 'test'.
lines.metric: Count of all matching commit rows; repos deduplicated first so a commit is counted once per repo.
lines.sources: github_repos_languages.language_description for language, github_repos_licenses.license for license, github_repos_commits.message for commit text.

lines.keys: Exact repo_name match between the commit counts and the language rows. Languages are first limited to repos that have commits. An inner join drops repos with no language row.
lines.rank: Sort by commit count, highest first, with no tie-break, and keep the top 5.
lines.parse: Regex on language_description: the text after the first ' in ' or ':' and before ' (N bytes' (commas allowed in N) or ', totaling' is taken as the main language.
lines.shape: Up to five rows with columns repo_name and num_commits; the question asks for names only, so the count column is extra. No rounding.
lines.filter: Keep a repo only if its parsed main language is not equal to 'Python'. A repo with a NULL parse result is also dropped.
lines.metric: Count of commit rows per repo_name, grouped over all of github_repos_commits.
lines.sources: github_repos_commits gives commit rows per repo_name; github_repos_languages.language_description is free text naming each repo's main language.

lines.keys: Reviews are joined to businesses on gmap_id with an exact match on both sides, no transformation needed.
lines.rank: Sort by average rating from highest to lowest and keep the first 5. No tie-break is set.
lines.parse: The city is read from description text with a word-bounded regex for 'Los Angeles, ' followed by either 'CA' or 'California'.
lines.shape: Up to five rows with the business name and its average rating, unrounded.
lines.filter: Keep only businesses whose description matches that Los Angeles pattern, so neighbouring cities are excluded. There is no time window and no HAVING.
lines.metric: The unrounded mean of review.rating across individual reviews, grouped per business by gmap_id and name.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description gives name and the prose description that holds the location; googlelocal_review gives each review's rating.

lines.keys: Reviews match businesses on an exact gmap_id equality, with no transformation on either side.
lines.rank: Sorted by the numeric average rating, highest first. There is no tie-break and no limit.
lines.parse: Case-insensitive regex with word boundaries: the name contains 'massage', or the description mentions bodywork, body treatment(s), therapy/therapies/therapist(s)/therapeutic, or a word starting with 'massag'.
lines.shape: Many rows with two columns: name, and the average rating rounded to 15 decimals and cast to text.
lines.filter: A business counts if the name or the description matches. After grouping, only businesses with an average rating of at least 4.0 are kept (inclusive).
lines.metric: Mean of review ratings for each business, grouped by gmap_id and name.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description supplies gmap_id, name and the free-text description. googlelocal_review supplies the per-review rating.

lines.keys: Reviews join to businesses on gmap_id, an exact key. The rebuilt hours text and the evening set also join back on gmap_id.
lines.rank: Highest average rating first. Ties go to fewer reviews, then name ascending. Limit 5.
lines.parse: hours is cast to jsonb and expanded with ordinality. A regex reads 'open–close' (en dash), with optional minutes and an optional AM/PM on the open time that falls back to the close's. Times are converted to minutes; 'Open 24 hours' is kept as literal text.
lines.shape: Five rows with columns name, operating_hours text and the unrounded average rating.
lines.filter: Businesses with NULL hours are excluded. At least one Monday–Friday entry must be 'Open 24 hours', close after 18:00, or close at or before open (past midnight). A 6PM close does not count.
lines.metric: Average of review rating per qualifying business, plus a review count. The hours are rebuilt as one text list of [day, hours] pairs in stored order.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description gives name and the hours column, which is JSON text of [day, hours] pairs. googlelocal_review gives the rating for each review.

lines.keys: Reviews join businesses on an exact gmap_id match. Neither side needs any transformation first.
lines.rank: Sorts by count from high to low, breaks ties by name alphabetically, and keeps the top 3.
lines.parse: The review time text comes in three formats: ISO date-time, 'day Mon year, 24-hour time' and 'Month day, year at 12-hour time AM/PM'. A regex picks the format and to_timestamp parses it.
lines.shape: Returns three rows, each with the business name and its high-rating review count.
lines.filter: Keeps ratings of … or more, which means 5-star reviews because ratings are whole numbers. The parsed timestamp must fall between 1 Jan 2019 and 1 Jan 2020, start included and end excluded.
lines.metric: Counts the qualifying reviews for each business, grouped by gmap_id and name.
lines.sources: googlelocal_review supplies rating, time and gmap_id. googlelocal_business_description supplies the business name.

lines.keys: Sales join the matched song records on track_id. Records match when the folded song and artist keys are one deletion or less from the question's folded keys.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: Title unwrapped by source_id: 1 drops the trailing ' (Album)'; 2 splits 'Artist - Title' when artist is null; 3 keeps the part before ' - '; 4 drops the leading 3–4 digit prefix; 5 plain. Keys lower-cased, accents folded, non-alphanumerics removed.
lines.shape: One row, one column revenue_usd, rounded to 2 decimals.
lines.filter: Keep sales where store is 'Apple Music' and country is 'Canada'. Records count only when both song key and artist key match within one deletion.
lines.metric: Sum of revenue_usd over every sale of all duplicate records of the song, treated as one song.
lines.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks supplies title, artist, album and source_id for each song record; music_brainz_20k_sales supplies store, country and revenue_usd per track.

lines.keys: Sales join the matched track rows on track_id. All duplicate track records that resolve to the song are kept, so every variant's sales count.
lines.rank: Stores are ordered by summed revenue, highest first, limit 1. There is no tie-break.
lines.parse: Title and artist are reduced to lowercase letters only (non-letters stripped). The title key comes from the question's title; the surname key is the second word of the question's artist.
lines.shape: One row with a single column, the store name. No revenue value is output and there is no rounding.
lines.filter: A track counts when its normalized title contains the normalized title key and its normalized artist contains the normalized surname. There is no country or date restriction.
lines.metric: Sum of revenue_usd per store, over sales of all matched track rows.
lines.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks supplies title and artist to identify the song; music_brainz_20k_sales supplies store and revenue_usd per sale.

lines.keys: Duplicate tracks are clustered by resolved song and performer keys; each cluster is labelled with its smallest track_id. The sales table joins to cluster members on an exact track_id match.
lines.rank: Clusters are ordered by total revenue, highest first, and only the top one is kept. There is no tie-break.
lines.parse: The song is unwrapped per source: 1 strips a trailing ' (Album)', 2 takes the text after ' - ' and uses the text before it as the artist, 3 takes the text before ' - ', 4 strips a leading 3–4 digit prefix. Keys are lower-cased, accents folded, letters and digits only.
lines.shape: One column: the raw title of every record in the winning cluster. Many rows, ordered by track_id, with no rounding.
lines.filter: Records are dropped if their song or artist key is empty or the artist key is 'unknown'. No time window. One-typo matching (single-character deletions) only applies to keys of six or more characters.
lines.metric: Two records are linked when one key matches exactly and the other is within one deletion. Three rounds of minimum-label propagation form the clusters, then revenue_usd is summed per cluster label.
lines.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks gives title, artist, album and source_id for each duplicate record; music_brainz_20k_sales gives revenue_usd per track_id.

lines.keys: Barcode pulled from Patient_description matched exactly to ParticipantBarcode; expression rows restricted to Symbol equal to IGF2 inside the join condition.
lines.rank: Ordered by histology code ascending; no limit.
lines.parse: Barcode: first 'TCGA-' plus two-char and four-char alphanumeric segments. Disease: text after 'case of/subject with/diagnosed with/study of' up to comma or period, else 'belongs to the … cohort.', else leading 'In the … dataset,'.
lines.shape: One row per histology code: Histology_Type and Average_Log_Expression, unrounded full precision.
lines.filter: Disease equals 'Brain lower grade glioma'; histology code not null and not wholly enclosed in square brackets; normalized_count not null and greater than -1.
lines.metric: Average of base-10 log of (normalized_count + 1), grouped by ICD-O-3 histology code.
lines.sources: pancancer_atlas_clinical_info (Patient_description free text for barcode and disease; icd_o_3_histology as histology type); pancancer_atlas_rnaseq_expression (ParticipantBarcode, Symbol, normalized_count).

lines.keys: Barcode pulled from the clinical description by regex, left-joined on an exact match to the distinct mutation ParticipantBarcode; no case folding or prefix stripping.
lines.rank: Mutation fraction descending, ties broken by histological type ascending; limit 3.
lines.parse: Barcode is the first 'TCGA-' + two alphanumerics + '-' + four alphanumerics; vital status is the whole word Alive or Dead; BRCA means the description contains 'Breast invasive carcinoma'.
lines.shape: Three rows at most, with columns Histological_Type, mutation_count, total and mutation_percentage; the fraction is not rounded.
lines.filter: BRCA descriptions only; vital status Alive; histological_type not null; mutation side keeps only Hugo_Symbol CDH1 rows with FILTER 'PASS'.
lines.metric: For each histological type: distinct patients with a CDH1 PASS mutation, all alive patients, and the fraction mutated/total as a double (a 0–1 ratio, not multiplied by 100).
lines.sources: pancancer_atlas_clinical_info: Patient_description free text (barcode, vital status, cancer name) and histological_type; pancancer_atlas_mutation_data: ParticipantBarcode, Hugo_Symbol, FILTER.

lines.keys: Barcode pulled out of the clinical description matched exactly to mutation ParticipantBarcode through a left join, so patients with no mutation count as not mutated.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: From Patient_description: the first TCGA-XX-XXXX barcode pattern, the whole word MALE or FEMALE, and a text match on 'Breast invasive carcinoma' to mark BRCA.
lines.shape: One row, one column Chi2, a double precision number with no rounding.
lines.filter: BRCA, female, histological_type not null and not starting with a bracket; mutations limited to CDH1 with FILTER PASS, one row per patient. Cells dropped when their histology-row or mutation-column total is 10 or less.
lines.metric: Grid of every histology × mutated yes/no, with empty cells counted as zero. Chi-square sums (O−E)²/E over the kept cells, where E = row total × column total / N, recomputed after the drop.
lines.sources: pancancer_atlas_clinical_info (Patient_description free text for barcode, sex, cancer type; histological_type column); pancancer_atlas_mutation_data (ParticipantBarcode, Hugo_Symbol, FILTER).

lines.keys: Each code is cut to its first 4 characters (the subclass prefix) and matched exactly to patents_cpc_definition.symbol, where level is 5.
lines.rank: Per group, keeps the year with the highest EMA, taking the earliest year on ties. Output is sorted by group code ascending, with no limit.
lines.parse: The cpc text is cast to jsonb and its elements expanded. first is read as a boolean. The filing year is the first 4-digit run in filing_date, cast to integer.
lines.shape: A list with one column, cpc_group (the 4-character subclass code), one row per qualifying group.
lines.filter: Keeps only CPC entries flagged first=true and rows whose filing_date contains a 4-digit year, so 'None Date' rows are dropped. At the end, keeps groups whose best year equals 2022.
lines.metric: Counts patents per group per year, each patent once per group. Years run from the group's first to last year, with missing years set to zero. EMA starts at the first count; each later year is 0.2*count + 0.8*previous EMA, computed recursively.
lines.sources: patents_publicationinfo: cpc JSON array (code, first flags) and free-text filing_date; patents_cpc_definition: symbol and level identify level-5 groups.

lines.keys: The first three characters of each CPC code equal patents_cpc_definition.symbol, restricted to level 4. No other join.
lines.rank: For each group, pick the year with the highest EMA; ties go to the earliest year. Output is ordered by group code, with no limit.
lines.parse: Country is the two letters before the hyphen after 'publication number/pub. no.' in Patents_info. Year is the first four-digit run in the date text. Second-half month matched by name or abbreviation, case-insensitive. CPC codes come from the jsonb array elements where first is true.
lines.shape: One row per level-4 group: the full title, the group code and the best year. No rounding.
lines.filter: Keep rows where the country is DE, the grant year is 2019 and the grant month is July to December. The filing date must contain a year, which drops 'None Date'. Only primary CPC codes count.
lines.metric: Each patent counts once per level-4 group, and filings are counted per group and filing year. Missing years between the first and last are filled with zero. A recursive EMA starts at the first year's count, then 0.1*n + 0.9*previous.
lines.sources: patents_publicationinfo: Patents_info text (publication number), grant_date and filing_date text, cpc JSON array; patents_cpc_definition supplies titleFull by symbol and level.

lines.keys: Citation element publication_number matched exactly to the UC publication number parsed from Patents_info; citing primary CPC's 4-character code prefix matched to definition symbol at level 5.
lines.rank: Ordered by citing assignee, then subclass title; no limit.
lines.parse: Assignee is either the text before 'holds the XX (patent) application/filing (' or the text after owned by/assigned to/held by/belonging to, before 'and has'/', with' publication no.; publication number is the sentence's final ID.
lines.shape: Many rows: citing assignee and titleFull, with the title wrapped in CSV-style double quotes (inner quotes doubled) when it contains a comma or quote.
lines.filter: Cited patents have assignee exactly UNIV CALIFORNIA (LIKE prefilter first); citing rows have a non-empty citation array; only CPC elements with first true; citing assignee not exactly UNIV CALIFORNIA.
lines.metric: No aggregate; distinct citing publications, then distinct pairs of citing assignee and primary CPC subclass.
lines.sources: patents_publicationinfo: Patents_info sentence (assignee, publication number), citation JSON array, cpc JSON array; patents_cpc_definition: symbol, level, titleFull for subclass titles.

lines.keys: The hand-written symbol map is joined to index_info on the exact exchange name. Only Asia symbols are kept, and trade rows are matched to them by Index.
lines.rank: Orders indexes by average volatility, highest first, and keeps the top one. There is no tie-break.
lines.parse: Date is text in three shapes: 'YYYY-MM-DD time', 'DD Mon YYYY, time' and 'Month DD, YYYY at time'. A regex picks the shape, then to_date reads only the date part.
lines.shape: One row with a single column, the index symbol. The average itself is not returned and nothing is rounded.
lines.filter: Keeps only indexes mapped to the Asia region whose exchange exists in index_info, and only trading days on or after 2020-01-01 (the start date is inclusive).
lines.metric: Each day's volatility is (High minus Low) divided by Open. These values are averaged per index symbol.
lines.sources: stockindex_index_trade gives daily Open, High, Low, Date and Index symbol; stockindex_index_info gives Exchange names. A hand-written VALUES list maps each symbol to its exchange and region.

lines.keys: The hand map's exchange name is inner-joined to index_info.Exchange by exact match. Trade rows are then kept when their Index is among the mapped North American symbols.
lines.rank: Sorted by Index ascending. No limit.
lines.parse: Date text comes in three shapes: ISO date plus time, 'DD Mon YYYY, time', and 'Month DD, YYYY at time'. A regex picks the shape, and to_date reads only the day part.
lines.shape: One column, the Index symbol, with one row for each qualifying North American index.
lines.filter: Keep only the symbols mapped to the North America region, and only parsed dates from 2018-01-01 up to but not including 2019-01-01.
lines.metric: Per index, count up days (Close greater than Open) and down days (Close less than Open). Flat days count as neither. HAVING keeps an index only when up days are strictly more than down days.
lines.sources: stockindex_index_trade gives Index, Open, Close and text Date. stockindex_index_info gives Exchange names. Region is not stored anywhere, so a hand-written values list maps symbols to exchange and region.

lines.keys: The trade Index is matched exactly to the lookup symbol. The lookup exchange name is matched exactly to index_info Exchange, so only exchanges spelled as stored are kept.
lines.rank: Sorted by last-to-first close ratio, highest first. Top 5 kept; no tie-break.
lines.parse: The text Date comes in three formats: ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss' (first ten characters), 'DD Mon YYYY, hh:mm' (first eleven characters), and 'Month DD, YYYY at …' (the part before ' at '). Each is chosen by a regex.
lines.shape: Five rows with two columns, Index symbol and Country, and no return value shown.
lines.filter: Keeps only rows with a parsed date on or after 2000-01-01, and only indices whose symbol maps to a matched exchange.
lines.metric: One value per index: buy-and-hold return, the Close on its latest date divided by the Close on its earliest date. This is not a monthly-investment (dollar-cost averaging) calculation.
lines.sources: stockindex_index_trade gives Index, Date and Close. stockindex_index_info gives Exchange names. A hand-written values list maps each index symbol to its exchange and country.

lines.keys: stocktrade_all."_table" is matched to the stockinfo Symbol after the Symbol is lower-cased.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: The company is found by a prefix match: the description starts with the company's full name. "Date" is text in YYYY-MM-DD form, so it is compared as a string.
lines.shape: One row with one column, max_adj_close, not rounded.
lines.filter: Keep only trade rows whose Date string is on or after the first day of 2020 and before the first day of 2021.
lines.metric: The maximum of "Adj Close" across the company's daily rows in 2020.
lines.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo gives the company's Symbol through its "Company Description" text; stockmarket_stocktrade_all has the daily rows with "Adj Close", "Date" and a "_table" ticker column.

lines.keys: A trade row's ticker (the _table value, or the literal table name for the extra tables) matches the lowercased stockinfo Symbol exactly.
lines.rank: ETF rows come first, sorted by Symbol, and the total row comes last. There is no limit.
lines.parse: The name is the start of Company Description, cut before the first ', <lowercase letter>' clause or before a listed verb (offers, is, provides, invests…), with trailing commas and spaces trimmed. The 2015 dates are picked by the text prefix of Date.
lines.shape: One column (name): one row per ETF with its parsed name, then one final row with the total count.
lines.filter: Keep rows where ETF is 'Y' and Listing Exchange is 'P' (NYSE Arca), and at least one 2015 price row has Adj Close strictly greater than 200, tested with EXISTS.
lines.metric: Each qualifying ETF is listed once. Qualifying ETFs are counted with count(*), shown as the text 'Total: ' followed by the number.
lines.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo gives Symbol, ETF flag, Listing Exchange and Company Description. Prices come from the stored union stockmarket_stocktrade_all plus 38 per-ticker tables with double-precision Volume, each added by name.

lines.keys: Each volume row is tagged with its ticker (the stored _table column, or a literal name). It is matched to the lowercased stockinfo Symbol.
lines.rank: Ordered by Symbol ascending; no limit.
lines.parse: The company name is the lead of Company Description, cut before the first ', lowercase' clause or listed verb such as 'is' or 'provides'. Periods are removed and trailing commas and spaces trimmed. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD text.
lines.shape: Many rows, two columns: the parsed company name and the average daily 2008 volume, rounded to 2 decimals.
lines.filter: Market Category is Q, G or S (NASDAQ); Financial Status is D, E or H (deficient, delinquent, both); Date starts with '2008'; Volume is not null.
lines.metric: Average of Volume cast to float, per company (grouped by Symbol and parsed name), over its non-null 2008 daily rows. The inner join keeps only companies with 2008 volume.
lines.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo gives Symbol, Market Category, Financial Status and the free-text Company Description; volumes come from stockmarket_stocktrade_all plus 38 per-ticker tables with double-precision Volume.

lines.keys: stocktrade_all._table is matched to the lower-cased stockinfo Symbol.
lines.rank: Order by up days minus down days, highest first, ties broken by ticker ascending; take the top 5.
lines.parse: Company name = start of Company Description: first word, then words that don't start lower-case or are connectors (of, and, the, plc...), stopping at other lower-case word; trailing period/comma removed. Date compared as 'YYYY-MM-DD' text.
lines.shape: A single column of company names, up to five rows, with no symbols or counts.
lines.filter: Listing Exchange 'N' (NYSE) and ETF 'N'; trade dates from 2017-01-01 up to but not including 2018-01-01; keep tickers whose up days strictly exceed their down days.
lines.metric: For each ticker, count days where Close > Open (up days) and days where Close < Open (down days); days where they are equal are not counted.
lines.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo gives Symbol, Listing Exchange, ETF flag and Company Description (the name comes from this); stockmarket_stocktrade_all gives daily Open, Close and Date, with each ticker tagged in _table.

lines.keys: Trades match companies when the trade table's _table equals the lower-cased stockinfo Symbol.
lines.rank: Wide-range day count descending, ties broken by ticker ascending, limit 5.
lines.parse: Company name comes from Company Description: first word, then words starting non-lowercase or connectors (of, and, the, plc…), stopping at other lowercase words; trailing period/comma removed.
lines.shape: One column, company_name, with five rows; the counts are not shown.
lines.filter: Only Market Category 'S' (NASDAQ Capital Market); Date text from 2019-01-01 up to but not including 2020-01-01; days where High minus Low is strictly greater than 0.2 times Low.
lines.metric: Count of qualifying trade days per ticker, grouped by _table.
lines.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo gives Symbol, Market Category and Company Description; stockmarket_stocktrade_all gives daily High, Low and Date, with each row tagged by its ticker in _table.

lines.keys: yelp_review.business_ref matches yelp_business.business_id on the numeric suffix: the 'businessref_' and 'businessid_' prefixes are removed before the equality comparison.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: The city and state are read by a case-insensitive substring match for 'Indianapolis, IN' anywhere in the description text.
lines.shape: One row with a single unrounded average value.
lines.filter: Only reviews of businesses whose description contains 'Indianapolis, IN', matched case-insensitively. No time window and no other exclusions.
lines.metric: The plain average of review rating across every matching review, pooled over all Indianapolis businesses, so it is weighted by review count and not averaged per business.
lines.sources: yelp_business.description holds the location inside templated text; yelp_review.rating holds the ratings, since businesses have no star column.

lines.keys: business_id has its 'businessid_' prefix swapped for 'businessref_' to match yelp_review.business_ref exactly; the extracted state code is matched to the US code list.
lines.rank: States ordered by review count descending, ties broken by state code alphabetically; keep top 1.
lines.parse: State code is the first two-capital-letter word after a comma and space in description, ending at a word boundary; this works for all lead phrasings.
lines.shape: One row: the state code and its unrounded average rating; the review count is not output.
lines.filter: Only businesses whose extracted code is a US state or DC are kept (e.g. Canadian province codes dropped); inner joins also drop reviews without a matched business.
lines.metric: Per state: count of review rows, and the mean rating over all reviews pooled together (rating cast to float), not an average of business averages.
lines.sources: yelp_business.description holds the location text containing the state code; yelp_review holds one row per review with rating and business_ref; a hand-written list of 50 US state codes plus DC.

lines.keys: In review business_ref, the 'businessref_' prefix is replaced with 'businessid_' so it matches yelp_business.business_id exactly. Reviewed businesses are made distinct before the join.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: The review date comes in three shapes, each matched by a regex and read with its own format: ISO date-time, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH:MI', and 'Month DD, YYYY at HH:MI AM/PM'. BusinessParking is a Python-style dict string whose key/True-False-None pairs are pulled out by regex, allowing an optional u prefix.
lines.shape: One row with a single count column named businesses.
lines.filter: Keep reviews timestamped from 2018-01-01 up to but not including 2019-01-01. Keep businesses where BikeParking is exactly 'True', or where any BusinessParking kind is True. A missing attribute counts as false.
lines.metric: Count the distinct reviewed businesses that meet either parking condition.
lines.sources: yelp_review supplies business_ref and the text date column. yelp_business supplies business_id and the attributes JSON, with its BikeParking and BusinessParking keys.

lines.keys: Review business_ref matched to business_id after replacing the 'businessid_' prefix with 'businessref_'; categories are matched by exact text.
lines.rank: Order categories by business count, highest first, with ties broken alphabetically by category; keep the first one.
lines.parse: Take the text after the ', ST' state code, split on commas, pull every Title-Case run (joined by space, ' & ', ' of ', with parentheses allowed); bare lowercase segments are title-cased too.
lines.shape: One row with the category name and its average rating, unrounded.
lines.filter: Only businesses whose BusinessAcceptsCreditCards attribute equals the string 'True'. Businesses with 'False' or no attribute are left out.
lines.metric: Count distinct businesses per category. For the top category, average all review ratings of its credit-card businesses as floats.
lines.sources: yelp_business.description holds categories inside prose; yelp_business.attributes JSON holds BusinessAcceptsCreditCards; yelp_review.rating and business_ref give review ratings.

lines.keys: Numeric suffix: strip 'businessid_' from business_id and 'businessref_' from review business_ref, then match the remaining text exactly.
lines.rank: States ordered by WiFi business count descending, ties broken alphabetically by state code, limit 1.
lines.parse: WiFi value read from attributes->>'WiFi', with any leading u', leading quote and trailing quote removed. State is the first two-capital-letter code after a comma-space in description.
lines.shape: One row: state code and average rating rounded to 2 decimals.
lines.filter: Keep businesses whose cleaned WiFi value is free or paid; drop 'no' and missing. Leave out Canadian province codes when choosing the state.
lines.metric: Count WiFi businesses per state to choose the top state, then average review rating across all reviews of that state's WiFi businesses.
lines.sources: yelp_business: attributes JSON (WiFi key) and description text (holds city/state); yelp_review: rating per review, linked by business_ref.

lines.keys: Strip 'businessref_' from the review's business_ref and 'businessid_' from the business's business_id, then match the remaining numeric text exactly.
lines.rank: Order by average rating descending, then review count descending, then business number ascending. Keep only the top one.
lines.parse: Review dates come in three shapes, each chosen by a regex: ISO datetime, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI', or 'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM'. Categories are the capitalised phrases after the 'City, ST,' clause.
lines.shape: One column, one row: the business name followed by its categories in the order they appear, joined by ', '.
lines.filter: Keep reviews dated from 2016-01-01 up to but not including 2016-07-01. HAVING keeps businesses with at least 5 reviews in that window.
lines.metric: Per business number: average rating and count of reviews inside the window.
lines.sources: yelp_review supplies business_ref, rating and the text date; yelp_business supplies name and description, and categories are read out of the free-text description.

lines.keys: Reviews join users on user_id. Review business_ref and business business_id match after dropping their 'businessref_' and 'businessid_' prefixes to get a bare number.
lines.rank: Review count from highest to lowest, ties broken alphabetically by category, top 5 kept.
lines.parse: Dates come in three text formats, each matched by regex and parsed with to_timestamp. Categories are the capitalised phrases after the 'City, ST,' clause, joined by space, '&', '/', 'of', with '(X)' qualifiers.
lines.shape: Five rows, one column: the category name. Counts are not shown.
lines.filter: Users whose parsed yelping_since year is 2016. Reviews dated on or after 2016-01-01. Reviews with no user or no matching business drop out of the inner joins.
lines.metric: Counts reviews per category. Each distinct (business, category) pair is counted once, so every review adds 1 to each category of its business.
lines.sources: yelp_user.yelping_since for registration date; yelp_review.date, user_id, business_ref for reviews; yelp_business.description free text holds the categories.

agent.sources: deps_dev_v1_packageinfo (System, Name, Version, UpstreamPublishedAt, VersionInfo JSON); deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion for ProjectName; deps_dev_v1_project_info.Project_Information free text for repo and stars.
agent.keys: Versions match project_packageversion on System NPM, Name and Version exactly; lowercased ProjectName matches lowercased owner/repo token read from Project_Information.
agent.parse: VersionInfo Ordinal cast to int and IsRelease cast to boolean; owner/repo is the first slug token; stars from 'stars count of N', 'N stars', or 'starred by N users', with commas removed.
agent.filter: NPM release rows only; the latest per package is picked by UpstreamPublishedAt descending, then Ordinal, then Version; the joins drop packages with no matching project.
agent.metric: Per package, keep the matched project row with the highest stars (row_number), which is the same as taking the max stars.
agent.rank: Order by stars descending (nulls last), then Name ascending to break ties; limit 5.
agent.shape: Five rows with Name, Version and an extra stars column.

deps_dev_v1/1.why: Many lodash packages tie for 5th place at the same star count, and the agent breaks the tie by Name ascending where the reference uses Name descending, so a different package ends up 5th.

agent.sources: github_repos_contents alone gives the README text along with its sample_repo_name and sample_path; github_repos_files is not used. github_repos_languages.language_description gives each repo's languages.
agent.keys: Non-Python repos join contents on the exact sample_repo_name, not through files on the blob id. Rows are made distinct by blob id.
agent.parse: Python is found as a token: 'Python' followed by ' (' or ', totaling'. Copyright is a case-insensitive substring match on 'copyright' only, without the © symbol.
agent.filter: Keep a sample_path only if it ends in 'README.md' (case-sensitive LIKE with no directory boundary). The repo must have a languages row, and none of its rows may match Python.
agent.metric: Each distinct blob counts once. The metric is the average of a 0/1 copyright flag, which gives the proportion directly.
agent.shape: One row with one column: the proportion rounded to 4 decimals, without the total or copyright counts.

github_repos/1.why: The agent picks README files from the contents table's sample_repo_name and sample_path, not from the files table joined to contents on the blob id, so it counts a different set of README rows.

agent.sources: pancancer_atlas_clinical_info: Patient_description free text and histological_type; pancancer_atlas_mutation_data: ParticipantBarcode and Hugo_Symbol (FILTER column not used).
agent.keys: Barcode pulled from description by regex, left-joined on exact match to distinct mutation ParticipantBarcode.
agent.parse: Barcode is first TCGA-XX-XXXX pattern; alive is a case-insensitive whole-word match; BRCA is a case-insensitive substring match on 'breast invasive carcinoma'.
agent.filter: BRCA, alive, histological_type not null and not a bracketed placeholder; mutation side keeps all CDH1 rows with no FILTER='PASS' condition.
agent.metric: Per histological type: distinct mutated patients over all alive patients, multiplied by 100 as a percentage.
agent.rank: Percentage descending, ties broken by histological type ascending; limit 3.
agent.shape: Three rows with histological_type and percentage rounded to 2 decimals; no mutation_count or total columns.

pancancer_atlas/2.why: The agent counts every CDH1 mutation row without requiring FILTER = 'PASS', so more patients count as mutated (for example, lobular carcinoma comes out near 50% instead of about 42%).

agent.sources: bookreview_books_info (book_id, details prose only, no subtitle fallback); bookreview_review (purchase_id, rating).
agent.keys: Trailing digits pulled from book_id and purchase_id and cast to int; the tables are joined on that number.
agent.parse: Year = four digits after the first month name, allowing whitespace, an optional day and comma, read from details only; subtitle is not used as a fallback.
agent.filter: Books with no parsed decade are dropped; the inner join keeps only reviewed books; HAVING keeps decades with at least 10 distinct books.
agent.metric: Decade = year integer-divided by 10, times 10. Per decade: mean rating over individual reviews.
agent.rank: Ordered by average rating, highest first, with decade as tie-break; limit 1.
agent.shape: One row, two columns: the decade as text with an 's' suffix (e.g. '2020s') and the average rating, unrounded.

bookreview/1.why: The agent returns the decade as text with an 's' suffix ('2020s') rather than the integer 2020, and adds an extra avg_rating column; it also skips the subtitle fallback, but that does not change which decade wins.

agent.sources: voicecalltranscript__c Body__c, product2 with pricebookentry UnitPrice, knowledge__kav faq_answer__c; the lead table is not read.
agent.keys: Transcript LeadId__c trimmed and '#' stripped compared to literal; pricebookentry to product on normalised ids; products and article cross-joined, not matched to call text.
agent.parse: none; policy answer returned whole, not split into numbered rules; no product-name search in transcript.
agent.filter: Given lead's transcripts; product name ILIKE a hardcoded product; one hardcoded knowledge article id.
agent.shape: One wide row per combination: transcript body, product name, unit price, full policy text; no lead row, no kind/ref_id columns.

crmarenapro/1.why: The agent never reads the lead table, so the lead's name, title, company and status are missing from its output.

agent.sources: quotelineitem for lines, product2 for names, pricebookentry for list price; knowledge__kav faq_answer__c body with title and summary.
agent.keys: Line items join product2 and pricebookentry by Id with '#' and spaces stripped; quote id matched exactly after the same cleanup.
agent.parse: No splitting: each article body returned whole. Quantity, prices, discount and total left as text and concatenated.
agent.filter: Only this quote's lines. Articles where summary equals title, summary starts with 'Policy', or title mentions quantity limit; no product-relevance filter on rules.
agent.metric: none: no aggregation; lists lines and whole articles as evidence.
agent.shape: Many rows, three columns: kind, label (product or article id plus title), detail (pipe-joined numbers or full body text).

crmarenapro/2.why: The agent returns each article's whole body instead of splitting it on blank lines into numbered rule paragraphs, so its rows do not match the reference's one-row-per-rule evidence.

agent.sources: crmarenapro_opportunity supplies Id and StageName; crmarenapro_task supplies WhatId, Subject, Status, ActivityDate, Description. Task Id, opportunity Name and CloseDate are not read.
agent.keys: task.WhatId joined to opportunity.Id, both trimmed and stripped of leading '#'.
agent.parse: No extraction; only task Status is trimmed, Subject and Description left untrimmed, StageName raw without prefix.
agent.filter: Only the opportunity whose normalised Id equals the given id, with all its linked tasks; no date or status exclusions.
agent.metric: No aggregate; plain join repeating the stage on every task row, no separate opportunity evidence row.
agent.rank: Tasks ordered by activity date ascending, no tie-break, no limit.
agent.shape: Many rows with columns StageName, subject, status, activity_date, description; no kind or id column.

crmarenapro/3.why: The agent never reads the task Id or the opportunity's Name and CloseDate. As a result, it has no id column and no stacked opportunity evidence row, and it also leaves Subject untrimmed.

agent.sources: quotelineitem for quantity, prices, discount, total; product2 for names; pricebookentry for list price; knowledge__kav title, summary and faq_answer__c.
agent.keys: Line items joined to product and pricebook entry by Id with spaces trimmed and leading '#' stripped; quote id cleaned the same way.
agent.parse: No parsing: quantities and prices left as text, article body returned whole, not split into numbered rule paragraphs.
agent.filter: Keeps line items of the given quote; articles whose summary equals title or starts with 'Policy' (case-sensitive LIKE); no filter on rules naming quote products.
agent.metric: none; every line item is cross-joined with every policy article, no aggregation
agent.rank: Ordered by article id, then product name; no limit.
agent.shape: Many rows: line-item columns repeated alongside article id, title and full article text on every row.

crmarenapro/6.why: The agent never splits the article body into numbered rule paragraphs. It returns each article's full text, so it cannot keep only the rules that apply to this quote's products.

agent.sources: crmarenapro_opportunity (OwnerId as agent, Amount, ContractID__c) and crmarenapro_contract (Id, CompanySignedDate); no order or order item tables.
agent.keys: Opportunity matches contract on contract id, both trimmed with leading '#' stripped.
agent.parse: CompanySignedDate cast directly to date without trimming; Amount text cast to numeric.
agent.filter: Company signed date from 2022-06-25 up to and including 2022-11-25.
agent.metric: Sum of opportunity Amount per opportunity owner.
agent.rank: Sum descending, ties by owner id ascending, limit 1.
agent.shape: One row, one column: the owner id.

crmarenapro/13.why: The agent measures sales with opportunity Amount and opportunity owners, not with order owners and the sum of order item quantity times unit price.

agent.sources: googlelocal_business_description for name and hours JSON text; googlelocal_review for ratings.
agent.keys: Qualifying businesses, business table and per-business review averages joined on gmap_id, an exact key.
agent.parse: hours cast to json and expanded. A regex reads 'open–close' with optional minutes and an optional open AM/PM that falls back to the close's. Times are converted to minutes.
agent.filter: NULL hours excluded. At least one Mon–Fri entry must be 'Open 24 hours' or close after 18:00, where a close at or before open gets 24h added (past midnight).
agent.metric: Average review rating per business, computed over all reviews and then joined to the qualifying businesses. No review count.
agent.rank: Average rating descending, ties broken by gmap_id, limit 5.
agent.shape: name, the raw stored hours text, and the average rounded to 2 decimals and cast to text.

googlelocal/3.why: The agent returns the raw stored hours JSON text (double-quoted) instead of the rebuilt [day, hours] list with single quotes, and it rounds the rating to text '5.00' instead of leaving it unrounded, so the column values don't match even though both return the same five businesses.

agent.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks for title, artist, album, source_id; music_brainz_20k_sales for revenue_usd per track_id.
agent.keys: Records grouped by exact (song key, artist key) pair, with no typo tolerance or clustering; sales pre-summed per track_id and joined on an exact track_id.
agent.parse: Per source: 1 strips ' (album)' built from the album column, 2 takes text after ' - ' and uses text before as artist, 3 drops the last ' - ' segment, 4 strips a leading digits-dash prefix. Keys keep letters only, lower-cased, no accent folding.
agent.filter: Only rows with an empty song key are dropped; the artist key may be empty or 'unknown'. No time window.
agent.metric: Revenue summed per exact (song key, artist key) group; a display title is picked from source 5 first, otherwise the lowest source.
agent.rank: Ordered by total revenue descending, tie-break on song key, limit 1.
agent.shape: One row with two columns: the chosen song title and total revenue rounded to 2 decimals.

music_brainz_20k/3.why: Both statements pick the same winning song, but the agent returns one row with a single chosen title plus rounded revenue, while the reference lists the raw title of every duplicate record in the cluster, in track_id order.

agent.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo, with NASDAQ read from the Listing Exchange column rather than Market Category; volumes from stockmarket_stocktrade_all plus only two double-precision tables (ftft, ftr), leaving out the other 36.
agent.keys: Each volume row is tagged with its ticker (the _table column, or a literal name) and matched to the lowercased stockinfo Symbol.
agent.parse: The name is cut from Company Description before the first ', lowercase' or listed verb (no 'offer' form). Spaces and trailing commas are trimmed, but periods are kept. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD text.
agent.filter: Listing Exchange = 'Q'; Financial Status is D, E or H; Date falls between 2008-01-01 and 2009-01-01; volume is not null.
agent.metric: Average of Volume cast to float, per Symbol and parsed name, over non-null 2008 rows; the inner join keeps only companies with volume.
agent.rank: Ordered by Symbol ascending; no limit.
agent.shape: Many rows, two columns: the company name and the average volume, not rounded.

stockmarket/3.why: The agent finds NASDAQ companies through the Listing Exchange column instead of Market Category Q/G/S, which drops …, and it unions only 2 of the 38 double-volume tables. It also keeps the periods in names and does not round the averages.

agent.sources: stockinfo for Symbol, exchange, ETF flag and Company Description; trades from stocktrade_all plus 14 separate per-ticker tables combined with UNION ALL.
agent.keys: The ticker tag on the trade rows is matched to the lower-cased stockinfo Symbol.
agent.parse: Name = description with everything cut off from the first listed verb (is, provides, operates...) or from a comma before a lower-case word; only trailing commas and spaces are trimmed, so a trailing period stays. Year taken with a LIKE '2017%' match on Date.
agent.filter: Listing Exchange 'N', ETF 'N', dates in 2017; keep tickers whose up days are greater than their down days (HAVING).
agent.metric: For each symbol, the sum of days with Close > Open and the sum of days with Close < Open.
agent.rank: Order by up days minus down days, highest first, ties broken by Symbol; take the top 5.
agent.shape: Three columns: the name, the up-day count and the down-day count; five rows.

stockmarket/4.why: The agent's name extraction keeps the trailing period (for example 'Inc.' and 'Ltd.'), while the reference removes it, so the name values don't match even though the same companies come out in the same order.

agent.sources: stockmarket_stockinfo for Symbol, Market Category, Company Description; stockmarket_stocktrade_all for High, Low, Date and _table ticker.
agent.keys: Trade _table joined to lower-cased stockinfo Symbol.
agent.parse: Company name cut from Company Description before a listed verb word (offers, is, provides...) or a comma followed by lowercase; only trailing commas/spaces are trimmed, so a trailing period stays.
agent.filter: Market Category 'S'; Date text starting with '2019'; High minus Low strictly greater than 0.2 times Low.
agent.metric: Count of qualifying trade days per ticker, grouped by _table.
agent.rank: Day count descending, ties broken by Symbol ascending, limit 5.
agent.shape: Two columns: company_name and the wide-range day count; five rows.

stockmarket/5.why: The agent cuts the name off before a fixed list of verbs and trims only trailing commas and spaces, so the period stays on names like 'Inc.'; the reference removes it.

agent.sources: yelp_business.description for categories, attributes JSON BusinessAcceptsCreditCards, yelp_review.rating via business_ref.
agent.keys: business_ref matched to business_id with the 'businessid_' prefix replaced by 'businessref_'; categories matched by exact text.
agent.parse: Take the text after the state code, then run one Title-Case regex over the whole tail without splitting on commas; bare lowercase list items are not read or title-cased.
agent.metric: Count distinct business-category pairs per category; for the top category, average all review ratings of its businesses.
agent.rank: Order by business count descending, then alphabetically by category; keep one.
agent.shape: One row with category, business count and average rating rounded to 2 decimals.

yelp/4.why: The agent never reads bare lowercase category items such as '…' and title-cases them, so some credit-card businesses are left out of … and the average changes (it is also rounded and comes with an extra count column).

agent.sources: yelp_review supplies business_ref, rating and text date; yelp_business supplies name and description, with categories read from the description.
agent.keys: Rewrite the review's 'businessref_' prefix to 'businessid_' and match business_id exactly.
agent.parse: Three date shapes chosen by regex (ISO, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI', 'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM' allowing 1-2 digit hour); categories are capitalised phrases after the state-code clause.
agent.filter: Reviews from 2016-01-01 up to but not including 2016-07-01; HAVING at least 5 reviews.
agent.metric: Per business_ref: average rating (count used only in HAVING).
agent.rank: Order by average rating descending, then business_ref text ascending; keep top one.
agent.shape: Three columns: business name, average rating rounded to 2, and categories joined by ', ' as a separate column.

yelp/6.why: The agent picks the same business, but returns its name, a rounded average rating and the categories as three separate columns. The reference returns one string: the name followed by the categories.
